races.name: Sky Sports Racing Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Elated
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 98 but has finished third in five of her last seven runs and never won over hurdles; hood headgear suggests temperament management is needed, and her hold-up style means she requires more pace than For Her Glory is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Third at Fontwell on her most recent start, stepping up in trip, she shows solid consistent form but remains without a win. Effective at today's distance and conditions, and first-time cheekpieces could provide the extra sharpness her debut form suggested she is capable of finding.

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton in the saddle for Dan Skelton is a powerful combination, and this mare already has a win on Good ground at 16f; prominent style suits tracking For Her Glory, and her T14 strike rate of 10/26 reflects a yard in form.
runners_data.comment: Progressive in bumpers with a win to her name, she switches to hurdles for a trainer in sparkling form who is striking at a high rate recently. Effective at today's distance and conditions, and her bumper ability suggests she is capable of making an impact in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Winters Hill
runners_data.note: Poor recent form with three consecutive finishes of 7th, 8th, and 8th, and flagged as a fader in the finish — her tendency to drop away late is a serious concern on Good ground where the race is likely to develop steadily before quickening; a hold-up position compounds her difficulties.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in her last three outings and yet to trouble the principals in any of them, she faces another stiff task here. First-time tongue-tie is added, but she requires significant improvement to be involved and is hard to recommend at this stage.

runners_data.name: For Her Glory
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen on a 4-year-old trained by Olly Murphy who has won at this exact trip on Good — she faces no pace rival and can dictate the tempo entirely on her own terms; her record of 1W2P from two starts on similar going is the most relevant stat in this race.
runners_data.comment: Third on her most recent start at Southwell after setting too strong a pace in a bumper, she had landed a debut win beforehand and ought to make further progress switching to hurdles. First-time hood may help her find a better rhythm; the key is whether she settles more readily.

runners_data.name: Likewhatyousee
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr aboard a mare with prominent-racing tendencies and placing form on Good at 17f; only one hurdle start to her name over this trip but bumper form suggests she handles Good and she has the scope to be competitive from a handy position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a neck on her hurdles debut here, outfought in the closing stages by a stronger and more experienced rival, she showed considerable ability and is expected to build on that. Effective at today's distance and conditions, she looks ready to take a forward step.

runners_data.name: Lundy View
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as such, with only two starts both finishing 6th and 7th on Good at 17f — James Davies rides for small yard Nigel Hawke (T14: 1/3) and this mare has yet to show she can compete with anything like these horses at this stage.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on both of her recent outings, she comes back after a break having failed to land a blow in a mares bumper here last time. Some improvement is possible as she switches to hurdles, but considerably more is required to be competitive in this field.

runners_data.name: Princess Of Ballea
runners_data.note: Four runs at 17f on Good give her the most course-relevant experience of the hold-up runners, and she has placed three times in recent form despite a stray U; Harry Reed rides for small yard Daisy Hitchins but the mare's jumping will need to be clean as she relies on a strong pace she is unlikely to get today.
runners_data.comment: Made little impression on her hurdles debut here most recently, detached throughout from an early stage, though she showed some promise in bumpers and runs in a first-time hood today. Usually held up, she is effective at today's distance and conditions; needs to demonstrate significantly more.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies takes the ride on this Anthony Honeyball runner who is placed on Good at 18f — the drop back slightly in trip from her best effort may be marginal, but her prominent style means she can compete for a handy position behind For Her Glory rather than relying on pace.
runners_data.comment: Showed ability in bumpers but struggled to adapt to hurdles on her debut here, making jumping errors throughout on her most recent start. First-time tongue-tie may sharpen her jumping, and there is underlying potential, though she remains a work in progress over obstacles.

races.paceDynamic: For Her Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Sean Bowen for Olly Murphy, is likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, uncontested gallop over this 2m1f Newton Abbot trip on Good ground. Getmyfriend, Likewhatyousee, and Steal A Glance will press forward in prominent positions, but none has the profile or inclination to seriously challenge For Her Glory for the lead, meaning the pace is set by one horse at a tempo she chooses. With no pace pressure, For Her Glory will conserve energy through the early stages and the race is unlikely to be truly run, favouring a horse that can travel close to the pace and quicken when it matters rather than one grinding from the back. This race shape clearly favours prominent-to-handy runners who can track the leader efficiently and pounce late, with deep hold-up types Elated and Princess Of Ballea carrying the most risk given they will need the pace to be genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If For Her Glory dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and simply outstays rivals from the front.
scenarios.body: If For Her Glory dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and simply outstays rivals from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Wear Leader Down
scenarios.trigger: If Getmyfriend or Likewhatyousee apply sustained pressure mid-race and For Her Glory ties up approaching the last.
scenarios.body: If Getmyfriend or Likewhatyousee apply sustained pressure mid-race and For Her Glory ties up approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace suddenly quickens from 3 out and the hold-up runners get a clear run to produce a late surge.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace suddenly quickens from 3 out and the hold-up runners get a clear run to produce a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Errors Shuffle Pack
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or market-movers refusing to settle cause positional chaos and open the race up from the back.
scenarios.body: If jumping errors or market-movers refusing to settle cause positional chaos and open the race up from the back.

watchPoints.text: For Her Glory (Bowen/Murphy) faces zero pace pressure and could exploit a lead role from flag to finish — watch whether any rival attempts to close the gap before the back straight or concedes the front entirely.

Winters Hill is flagged as a fader in the finish and has run 7th, 8th, 8th in her last three starts — if she is ridden prominently in an attempt to counter her finishing weakness, she could still stop quickly and cause interference at the hurdles.

Lundy View is lightly raced with only two runs on record and unknown jumping ability — watch early in the race for any hesitation or errors at the flight that could unsettle the field on the inside bend at Newton Abbot.

Getmyfriend (Skelton/Skelton, T14: 10/26) is the most dangerous market rival — monitor whether Harry Skelton presses the pace after jumping the third or conserves energy for a late challenge, as this choice significantly alters the race shape.

Likewhatyousee steps up markedly in experience from her single hurdle run — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr allows her to over-race early tracking For Her Glory, she may flatten out in the final half-mile and open the door for the hold-up runners.

races.name: Sun Racing Free Tickets With Sun Club Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kittys Glance
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, recently won twice at 20f on good ground and is on a career-high OR of 105 after a rapid rise; Tom Bellamy is an experienced partner and Alan King's yard is 3/12 in the 14-day window — uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage here.
runners_data.comment: First-time hood, and this mare has been building her profile over hurdles after a promising start in bumpers; she landed a race before a solid effort on handicap debut at Worcester three weeks ago, with trainer in fine current form.

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: Nick Slatter claims 3lb which offsets a natural hold-up style; showed back-to-back placed efforts at 16f on good ground in recent form and the step up to 2m2½f is worth monitoring given shortest starts were on a flat track — 45 days off should have freshened.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in his last three starts and moves into handicap company for the first time, which could unlock improvement; effective on sound ground, though composure in running will be key, and he has been off the track for 45 days.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old handicap veteran whose best recent form (2nd at 17f good) came at a comparable trip and surface; James Robottom's 10lb claim helps off OR 84, but Anthony Honeyball is 0/3 in the 14-day window and the horse's hold-up style means it must weave through a small field late.
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie applied for the first time on a mare who likes to force the pace; she showed encouragement when runner-up here recently, though she has blown hot and cold over hurdles and needs to find more consistency.

runners_data.name: Adaay Dancing
runners_data.note: Genuine rear-of-field galloper by inclination, though the field's shape means it is likely to find itself in a midfield berth rather than its natural position; Tom Broughton's 3lb claim is useful and the OR 82 mark is competitive, but a run of DNFs and beaten margins on soft/good suggests this trip and surface are still unproven territory.
runners_data.comment: First-time hood for a mare who likely found the ground faster than ideal when fourth at Huntingdon last time; she is at her best in easier conditions, remains unexposed, and there is more to come once things fall her way.

runners_data.name: Hawa Jumeirah
runners_data.note: Form string of 05-58 shows more misses than hits; the horse's natural hold-up tendency is squeezed by the field composition and Paul O'Brien faces the challenge of generating a run in a small field without a strong gallop to chase down — the sim-going record of 9/15 runs without a win on similar is a concern.
runners_data.comment: First-time tongue-tie for a gelding who carries Flat ability over the hurdles journey; he acts on today's going and trip, and while his opening handicap run here was below par, an improved show on a going day is not beyond him.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Callum Pritchard takes over a horse who has run five times on good ground recently without winning, though three placed efforts in that sequence show consistency; tongue-tie and cheekpieces are both in play, and the 10-day turnaround is notably quick — Joe Tickle is 1/12 in the 14-day window and Saucats's best form (2nd at 18f good) came at a comparable trip.
runners_data.comment: Tongue-tie and cheekpieces both first-time on a gelding who acts on today's going and trip; he made a sequence of jumping errors here last month and weakened, and though his mark may now be competitive, inconsistency remains the stumbling block.

runners_data.name: Katzoff
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — Dan Skelton's nine-year-old ran just three days ago and carries a pulsework flag; the sim-going record of 14/15 runs without a win on good is deeply uninspiring and the horse's redistribution from its natural hold-up position only adds to the difficulty of finding a winning shape.

races.paceDynamic: Kittys Glance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice handicap hurdle over 2m2½f on good ground at Newton Abbot, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Tom Bellamy can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Backer Bilk, Ask Peter, Adaay Dancing, Hawa Jumeirah, Saucats, and Katzoff are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the race devolves into a single leader setting an uncontested tempo against a cluster of closers who must make their ground from behind. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Adaay Dancing, Hawa Jumeirah, Saucats, and Katzoff are all true rear-of-field horses redistributed into midfield on the map, but Kittys Glance is the only runner realistically capable of controlling the early stages. This race shape — an uncontested leader on a fair surface — strongly favours the front-running profile: if Kittys Glance jumps cleanly and settles into a rhythm, the closest prominent trackers who can travel into contention from second or third are best placed, as pure hold-up runners face a stern task generating sufficient momentum from the back in a small field where the pace is unlikely to be truly severe.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kittys Glance Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Kittys Glance jumps cleanly, leads at a fair gallop and is never pressured for the lead.
scenarios.body: If Kittys Glance jumps cleanly, leads at a fair gallop and is never pressured for the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Trackers Overhaul Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kittys Glance's jumping is uneven or it flattens out in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If Kittys Glance's jumping is uneven or it flattens out in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Deep Closers Make Late Inroads
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is unexpectedly strong and the race develops into a proper test of stamina at 2m2½f.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is unexpectedly strong and the race develops into a proper test of stamina at 2m2½f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Through Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make significant jumping errors early, bunching the field and creating interference.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses make significant jumping errors early, bunching the field and creating interference.

watchPoints.text: Kittys Glance's jumping must be monitored from the first flight — a novice leading alone at Newton Abbot can drift into hurdles when fresh, and any error could hand momentum to the tracking hold-up horses.
Katzoff is listed as a NON-RUNNER — confirm before the off, as its absence reduces the field to six and tightens the pace picture further.
Saucats returns on a quick 10-day turnaround with both tongue-tie and cheekpieces — monitor in the paddock and early in the race for signs the equipment change sharpens or unsettles.

With four horses redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into a crowded midfield group, watch for traffic and interference at the top of Newton Abbot's home turn where the track narrows and bunching can cost momentum.|Adaay Dancing,Hawa Jumeirah

Backer Bilk and Ask Peter are the hold-up horses with the most recent good-ground placed form — if Kittys Glance begins to shorten stride approaching the last, these two are the likeliest beneficiaries and their finishing runs are worth tracking from the home straight.

races.name: St. Austell Brewery Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Northern Symphonie
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Harriet Dickin with a solid profile on Good ground (sim-going 7/15, 3W5P) and a proven route at 2m4f+; a 30-day break is not a concern for this handler, and blinkers suggest they want her sharper over a trip that suits her staying style.|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers as she switches back to hurdles — a more suitable test given her tendency to make errors at fences; effective at today's trip on decent ground. Winless in her last five outings and held at Warwick recently, she needs to improve.

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: The race-shaper here — Dan Skelton's yard is firing (T14: 13/29) and Harry Skelton will exploit the lack of pace pressure, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) and her best form coming in truly-run races means the lone lead is a double-edged sword if rivals time their runs well; headgear (p) unchanged.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces, and recent form is compelling: she landed a race before a close second on her stable debut off today's mark; effective at this trip on decent ground, and her trainer is among the form handlers at present.

runners_data.name: Hurst Hill
runners_data.note: Daniel Sansom (3lb claim) partners this Seamus Mullins-trained mare whose best form has come at distances around this mark and on Good and similar ground (sim-going 10/15, 1W4P); a natural hold-up type whose 21-day turnaround is straightforward, and her second over 2m4f on Good is the key piece of form.|
runners_data.comment: First-time blinkers for a mare who landed this contest last year and remains on a competitive mark; she could be building toward her best this season, though she was poorly placed off a slow pace when fourth here most recently.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes the ride on this Christian Williams five-year-old, but the horse's entire profile is built around racing from the rear over shorter trips (all five recent runs at 16f or less); the redistribution to midfield masks a true hold-up tendency, and this trip on this track is a significant test of whether the stamina is genuine at OR 80.|
runners_data.comment: Making a fresh start with a new yard, and her Southwell run last month can be treated as a debut effort for the stable; she acts on today's going, but has shown little under rules thus far and needs to show considerably more.

runners_data.name: Blue Siam
runners_data.note: Ellis Collier (5lb claim) rides this four-year-old, whose consistent mid-pack finishes (four of five finishing 3rd-5th) point to a horse who plugs on without ever quite firing; visor fitted, all Good-ground form, but the true hold-up style means she will be shuffled forward out of her comfort zone in a field this packed with similar types.|
runners_data.comment: First-time visor, and this filly has shown consistent placed form; she acts on today's going, though she ran too freely in front here last time and her effective range is shorter, so both settling and stamina are open questions.

runners_data.name: Ghost Jury
runners_data.note: Kayley Woollacott's mare has solid course-and-distance form on Good (sim-going 10/11, 0W2P) and Sean Bowen is a major jockey booking — the strongest pilot in this field outside Skelton; naturally a hold-up performer who will be pushed ahead of her preferred position, but Bowen's tactical ability may convert that compromise into a late threat.|
runners_data.comment: A point winner who has struggled to reproduce that level under rules; effective at today's trip and going, though she was comfortably held at Southwell last time despite holding a decent early position, and needs to find a better level.

runners_data.name: Bee's Kiss
runners_data.note: Jimmy Frost's six-year-old carries a hood and a difficult recent form line (P097-P) that includes two non-completions; good-ground form is limited (sim-going 3/6, 0W0P) and she has failed to see out trips beyond 2m in several recent starts — a concern at 2m5½f, particularly for a horse who will struggle to find natural cover at the rear with so many rivals sharing her style.|
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces for a mare with a point-to-point background who has shown nothing under rules so far; she went too freely in a chase here last month and was pulled up, and significant improvement will be needed over hurdles to feature.

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — if declared absent, this David Weston-trained five-year-old would have represented another genuine hold-up type crowded out of her natural role; her absence simplifies the traffic management at the back of the field marginally, though the problem of multiple closers versus one front-runner remains.|

races.paceDynamic: Miss Kassiopi is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with Harry Skelton aboard for the in-form Dan Skelton yard, she is expected to stride into an uncontested lead and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m5½f trip on Good ground. Behind her, the remainder of the field is overwhelmingly comprised of hold-up types — Northern Symphonie, Hurst Hill, Ghost Jury, Blue Siam, Global Hideaway, Bee's Kiss and At Sunrise all prefer to race from off the pace — meaning there will be no pressure on Miss Kassiopi early and the tempo is entirely in her hands. The field contains far more hold-up horses than the race map can honestly accommodate at the rear; Blue Siam, Global Hideaway and Ghost Jury are among those most likely to find themselves racing closer than ideal, but none are natural front-end threats to Miss Kassiopi's lead. This race shape strongly favours prominent/front-running types and, more specifically, any hold-up performer with a genuine late kick, as a controlled gallop risks not truly testing stamina and turning the race into a sprint from two out — making a well-timed, powerful closer the danger to the lone leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Kassiopi Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi breaks cleanly and settles into her rhythm without any rival disputing the lead.
scenarios.body: If Miss Kassiopi breaks cleanly and settles into her rhythm without any rival disputing the lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Closer Reels Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi sets only a modest gallop and a true staying hold-up type produces a powerful sustained run from the final bend.
scenarios.body: If Miss Kassiopi sets only a modest gallop and a true staying hold-up type produces a powerful sustained run from the final bend.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse in Final Hurdle
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi builds a big lead but is caught out by the long Newton Abbot run-in after setting a generous early gallop.
scenarios.body: If Miss Kassiopi builds a big lead but is caught out by the long Newton Abbot run-in after setting a generous early gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so gentle that the entire field arrives in a heap at the final hurdle with nothing separated.
scenarios.body: If the pace is so gentle that the entire field arrives in a heap at the final hurdle with nothing separated.

watchPoints.text: Miss Kassiopi's early jumping is critical — if she loses her lead at any of the first three hurdles, there is no second front-runner to take up the role and the race shape collapses entirely.|

Ghost Jury has Sean Bowen in the saddle — a significant jockey upgrade that could compensate for the hold-up horse being pushed forward out of her natural position; monitor whether Bowen elects to race closer than her style suggests.|

Northern Symphonie's rider Megan Bevan claims 7lbs, reducing her to an effective riding weight of 161lbs — watch whether the inexperience of a conditional jockey in a race with a lone front-runner compromises the timing of her challenge from the back.|

Blue Siam and Global Hideaway share almost identical racing profiles (true hold-up, OR 80-81, same jockey-claim range) and will likely compete for the same ground at the top of the home straight — if one tracks the other too closely, both risk getting boxed in on the turn.|

The Good ground at Newton Abbot today is consistent across all six races; no runner in this field has a meaningful Going CONCERN flag, meaning stamina and class differentials rather than ground suitability will be the decisive factor in the finish.|

races.name: Howden Insurance Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Duke Of Luckley
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here off a 31-day break, Martin Keighley's nine-year-old won over course and distance at Good last time and carries visor headgear; his high STYLE_FIT score of 0.92 reflects that he is operating in his lead role, and his course-going record (14 from 15 runs on similar ground) underlines his aptitude for conditions, though the weight of 168lbs is a consideration.|
runners_data.comment: Revived from a lengthy break to land a handicap by 15 lengths at Southwell last time off a 9lb lower mark, with a positive ride drawing the best from him. Proven at today's distance and conditions; the upward revision in the weights is the key question.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride on this six-year-old for Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies, who are 0/5 in the last 14 days, and Krak arrives on a 48-day absence having finished second over the same 2m trip at Good last time; his prominent style suits the expected race shape well and his form figures of 2/16f/GOO are directly relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Back in form and on a mark that looks workable against his best Irish figures, he shaped well when second on his final outing for his previous yard. Effective from 2m to 2m4f, he makes a promising stable debut for a trainer currently in good form.

runners_data.name: Schmilsson
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's six-year-old, who scored twice at this distance on Good ground in his last three runs, has been racing off a 343-day absence and his natural front-running style means he is squeezed into a midfield position on the map that does not reflect how he races; Sean Bowen may push forward early, but competing for space with Duke Of Luckley means his STYLE_FIT penalty of 0.93 is genuine and his race-fitness after nearly a year off is a live query.|
runners_data.comment: A winner at today's distance on similar ground last summer, he arrives in first-time cheekpieces after a lengthy absence and a below-par effort at Uttoxeter on his most recent start. The mark looks stiff given the modest level of last summer's wins, but there is scope to improve on latest.

runners_data.name: Gore Point
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners this Anthony Honeyball-trained six-year-old who ran just four days ago — an unusually quick turnaround — and whose three wins from his last six starts on Good ground speak to strong course-going aptitude; a true prominent type whose position at the rear of the map is an artefact of redistribution rather than his natural racing style, meaning he faces a significant positional challenge in a field full of similar pace preferences.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent in form and travelling particularly well last time, landing a handicap by 20 lengths at Stratford just four days ago off a 7lb lower mark. Proven at today's distance on similar ground and wears a tongue-tie for the first time; the revised mark is the one question.

races.paceDynamic: Duke Of Luckley is the lone confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and will set a controlled, uncontested tempo from the front, with Krak, Schmilsson, and Gore Point all natural prominent types who cannot all occupy their preferred early positions. Duke Of Luckley's recent winning form over course and distance at Good suggests he is well-placed to dictate a sustainable gallop, converting his lead role into a genuine stamina test rather than a sprint finish. The field holds more prominent types than it can accommodate — Schmilsson and Gore Point are both genuine prominent racers who have been redistributed into midfield and hold-up positions respectively, meaning neither is likely to secure their natural station with ease. This race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel comfortably just off a controlled pace and produce a clean jumping round, making compact prominent-to-lead profiles best positioned to exploit the uncontested tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duke Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Luckley leads at his own tempo and the field trails in an orderly queue throughout.
scenarios.body: If Duke Of Luckley leads at his own tempo and the field trails in an orderly queue throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Krak Picks Him Off
scenarios.trigger: If Krak travels smoothly in behind and reels in Duke Of Luckley after the last fence.
scenarios.body: If Krak travels smoothly in behind and reels in Duke Of Luckley after the last fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Schmilsson Forces Issue
scenarios.trigger: If Schmilsson pushes forward aggressively and forces a contested early pace that raises the tempo.
scenarios.body: If Schmilsson pushes forward aggressively and forces a contested early pace that raises the tempo.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Gore Point Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the leaders capitulate, allowing Gore Point to pick up the pieces from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or the leaders capitulate, allowing Gore Point to pick up the pieces from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Duke Of Luckley's uncontested lead could become dangerously comfortable — if he jumps fluently and sets a generous but not punishing gallop, no rival may have the tactical speed to reel him in from the positions they are forced into.

Schmilsson's 343-day absence is a significant fitness flag — Sean Bowen may have instructions to hunt a prominent position aggressively, but a horse returning from nearly a year off at a track that punishes errors under pressure is a real jumping-safety concern.

Gore Point raced only four days ago; connections clearly believe he is in top form, but any residual fatigue from that recent run could show late in a 2m½f handicap chase, particularly if he expends energy early fighting for a position against his redistribution.

With three of four runners genuine prominent types competing for the same early real estate, watch the first two fences closely — a crowded break or jumping mistake from any of Krak, Schmilsson, or Gore Point could reshape the entire race before it has settled.

The Good going is consistent across all Newton Abbot races today and appears genuinely fair; no going bias to exploit, meaning jumping accuracy and weight-carrying ability will be the primary differentiators in the straight.

races.name: Gordon Rowe Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Charlus
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse trained by Dan Skelton with Harry Skelton aboard, carrying a clear and flagged tendency to fade in the finish that is a genuine concern at this trip; recent form reads poorly (2FP0P) and a return from 84 days off adds a fitness query, though the Good ground suits on historical evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and off the course for 84 days, having been pulled up at Aintree on his most recent outing. The drop in class is notable and the trainer is in good form, but the mark remains stiff for a yard debut and today's ground is quicker than his best conditions.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's five-year-old has strong similar-going form (9/15, 2W4P) and shapes as the clear pace-maker here; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 is a minor flag that this race shape may see it marginally out of role, but in a field with no challenger for the lead it is most likely to secure the front position and dictate throughout.
runners_data.comment: Consistent over hurdles with a string of placed efforts, he filled the runner-up spot at Worcester last time beaten just 1½ lengths on a marginally lower mark. Effective at today's distance and conditions, and a flat track like Newton Abbot plays to his strengths; hard to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes takes the ride on this Ollie Pears-trained six-year-old who has a fine record on Good ground (11/15, 3W7P) and most recently won over the same 16f trip; returning from a 75-day break including a fall last time, jumping fluency will be monitored but the prominent style fits perfectly if Continuance sets an honest pace ahead.
runners_data.comment: Successful in this race 12 months ago, she comes here after a solid Flat effort and arrives at a venue that suits her front-running style on good ground. Effective at today's distance, she can cause real problems if given a clear lead from the outset.

runners_data.name: Arctic Voyage
runners_data.note: Michael Blake's lightly-weighted four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse who has won twice recently (1P1 in last three starts) over this trip and going, and arrives fit off a 30-day break; the profile suits a scenario where the pace quickens late, though in a steady-run race will need significant momentum from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Steadily progressive over hurdles with back-to-back wins before his most recent start, where he was eased through the closing stages when beaten a long way in a step up in class here. That performance can be excused; effective at today's distance and going, and should be sharper for it.

runners_data.name: Emerald Time
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy rides this Dom Elsworth & Ryan Hatch-trained five-year-old whose last run was a win 22 days ago over Good, giving it recency fitness; by nature a true hold-up horse shown in midfield on the map only because rear positions are crowded — the STYLE_FIT discount applies, and in a steadily run race without a true target to stalk, its chance is reduced.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap by 3 lengths at Worcester last time off a reduced mark, the tongue-tie retained after that success. Effective at today's distance and conditions, with more improvement potentially to come in handicaps; the rise for that success looks manageable.

races.paceDynamic: Continuance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rivals likely to contest the lead aggressively, is expected to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop from flag to finish over the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Max Of Stars is also a prominent racer and will likely track Continuance in second, creating a small lead group that sets a measured tempo rather than a searching one. With the pace modest and uncontested, the race is likely to develop into a test of jumping fluency and finishing reserves from the front, rather than a truly run stamina contest — a shape that strongly favours horses racing prominently who can control their own destiny. Emerald Time is a genuine hold-up type redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds more rear-division horses than the shape can naturally accommodate, with Charlus and Arctic Voyage the true closers most likely to occupy the rearward positions.

watchPoints.text: Watch Continuance's jumping — as the lone leader in a field of five on Good ground, any jumping error could immediately surrender its controlling advantage and dramatically shorten the race for the hold-up types.

Monitor whether Max Of Stars, returning from 75 days off including a fall (U in recent form), travels with confidence at the prominent pace — a jumping wobble early could leave Continuance unchallenged and the field strung out.

Arctic Voyage is the most dangerous closer in this field but needs a stronger-than-expected gallop to close the gap; if the pace is as moderate as expected, watch whether Harry Reed commits earlier than usual to compensate.

Charlus is flagged as a fader in the finish — if Harry Skelton elects to produce the horse slightly closer to the pace than its natural hold-up style to counteract this weakness, the move could change the complexion of the finish.

Emerald Time's true position in running is likely to be further back than the map indicates — watch where Tom Bellamy actually places the horse in the early stages as a guide to whether the stable has changed its tactical approach.

races.name: William Hill Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Great d'Ange
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old hold-up horse with solid good-ground form (13/15 sim-going), ridden by a 3lb claimer in Tom Broughton; form reads 35PP-9 and that run of pulled-ups warrants caution, though his best efforts have come over this sort of trip on this going.
runners_data.comment: A useful performer over fences, he arrives over hurdles having finished down the field at Stratford most recently in what appeared a conditioning run. Both a tongue-tie and visor appear on him for the first time; the going suits but others arrive here with considerably better recent form.

runners_data.name: Winning Paddy
runners_data.note: Trainer Alexandra Dunn has had one winner from four in the last 14 days suggesting current stable form; this horse won on good ground over 2m6f and has strong similar-going figures (4/5), but a natural hold-up style means he is reliant on a truly run race to get competitive late.
runners_data.comment: Won here by 8 lengths on his penultimate start and that course-and-distance form looks solid; his most recent run can be forgiven as he was caught in a slowly-run race that simply did not suit. First-time cheekpieces accompany him today and he is well suited by the extra distance on good ground.

runners_data.name: Longhouse Star
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for Stuart Curling but the horse hasn't run for 676 days — a massive flag — and while his best form came over staying trips, the very limited good-going record (0W0P in 1 run) and those recent soft-ground efforts mean he must prove residual ability before his tactical position even matters; his true style is off-the-pace despite appearing in midfield here.
runners_data.comment: With experience between the flags and now starting out for a new yard, he steps out in first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces having been pulled up on his most recent rules appearance in Ireland. The trainer is in good form and the break since then is a positive; however, he has plenty to prove under rules.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Kayley Woollacott's charge has been pulling-up in recent starts (32PP7-) and although his similar-going record (1W4P) is solid at face value, the form collapse combined with being shuffled into midfield against his natural rear-running instincts makes it hard to frame a case.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Taunton on his most recent hurdles return and back from a short break, he switches back to fences today which looks his better sphere. Effective at today's distance and conditions; the key question is whether he can produce a much-improved performance after a run of poor efforts.

runners_data.name: Daring Plan
runners_data.note: Most recent start produced a win (352-U1), Lucy Gardner retains the ride for a family yard, and the 20-day turnaround is tight but not alarming; suits good ground in principle, though this horse's natural off-the-pace style means the steady pace He Is A Cracker is likely to set will not be quick enough to bring him into play late.
runners_data.comment: Back to his best last time at Uttoxeter, grinding out a handicap victory by just over a length off a lower mark. Form has been inconsistent, but the confidence from that success could carry through; effective at today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: He Is A Cracker
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter, Barry Brennan's nine-year-old has been off 194 days and carries a 5lb claimer in Isabelle Ryder, which injects doubt about his ability to fully control tempo under pressure; that said, Good ground and a field of natural hold-up horses means he is virtually guaranteed an uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Off the track for over six months, having been pulled up at Fakenham last time on soft ground that did not suit him. He is a more reliable performer on sounder surfaces over fences, and today's conditions are more amenable; a tongue-tie is also added, though the lengthy absence remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Blackacre
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old for Mrs C Williams whose form reads 442F-5 with a fall in the mix; headgear (visor) applied, but the similar-going figures (1W3P across 7 runs) are modest, the 44-day break is manageable, and like several here he is a genuine rear-runner who the race shape does not naturally suit.
runners_data.comment: Below his best on his most recent hurdles start at Ffos Las, making jumping errors and well held throughout. He could be better suited returning to fences and the first-time visor is of interest; effective at the trip but needs to improve significantly on recent form to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Radharc Na Slaine
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is an elite booking for David Rees and this horse ran just 7 days ago — the quick turnaround is worth noting but Bowen rarely takes rides without purpose; a prominent style that will let him sit directly on He Is A Cracker's girth is the most naturally favoured position in this race shape, and his 13/15 similar-going record underlines his effectiveness on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Third most recently at Bangor-on-Dee, fading late back up in trip, beaten 3 lengths off his current mark. Effective at today's distance and suited by a sound surface, both of which apply here; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are added. Rated eighth of eight on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: He Is A Cracker is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with a 5lb claimer aboard in Isabelle Ryder, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 3m2f trip on Good ground — no rival is going to seriously dispute the lead with him. Radharc Na Slaine is the only other horse with a prominent profile and Sean Bowen will want to track closely, but the bulk of this field — Longhouse Star, Mcgregors Charge, Daring Plan, Blackacre, and the two hold-up horses Great d'Ange and Winning Paddy — are all genuine off-the-pace types who will be bunched in the chasing pack. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning Longhouse Star, Mcgregors Charge and Daring Plan are mapped to midfield but are unlikely to be racing in their true natural position. With a lone, unhurried front-runner setting a measured pace over a staying trip, the race shape strongly favours horses that can sit handy in the first pursuit group and travel powerfully — making Radharc Na Slaine's position just off the pace the most naturally advantaged profile, while genuine hold-up horses will need significant late stamina to bridge the gap.

watchPoints.text: He Is A Cracker carries a 5lb claimer (Isabelle Ryder) and hasn't run for 194 days — any signs of rustiness or jumping errors early could compromise his ability to control fractions and unravel the entire race shape.

Longhouse Star has been off 676 days; if Harry Skelton aggressively hunts a position forward to compensate for the lay-off, it could inject more pace into proceedings than the map anticipates and change the dynamic significantly.

Radharc Na Slaine ran only 7 days ago — watch in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of a horse not fully recovered, as a flat-footed early effort from Sean Bowen's mount would leave the prominent position unfilled and gift He Is A Cracker an even more comfortable lead.

With five genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield, there is a material risk of crowding and interference at the fences in the back straight — Blackacre (visor, fall in recent form) and Mcgregors Charge are the ones most likely to cause or suffer jumping disruption.
